It's very common for private landlords - not large corporate property managers, etc. - to get skittish about anything just because their profit margins are a lot thinner than a corporate property. Some are very, very picky and only approve apps from borderline perfect people. If your app's been approved and he's taken it off the market (confirm that with your realtor if you have one), then you probably have a little more leverage to negotiate the lease. That said, most leases I've seen for apartments are standard from the local realtors association. It's just a template. For him to modify it and add a clause he'd either have to write up a separate amendment to it, or write a whole new document, which is a PITA. Anyway, even with this clause lacking, the policy I've heard of is that you can move out and they will relist the unit, and you're responsible for renting the empty place until it's rented by another tenant. That's not as bad as the full year, assuming it gets interest and is rented by someone else within 1-2 months, but still not as great as being able to just show him a cool job offer and bow out early. That's a privilege generally only afforded at corporate properties that are comfortable with and adjusted to lots of turnover. **TL;DR** He probably won't screw you on it as-is, but you also don't want to sign something if you really, truly don't agree to it, so it's your call on how to proceed. All in all, if you really think you'll want to ditch because a cool job offer crops up, private renting may not be for you.
